question: T10: written and pushed before reading CAP-T10ROWS2. The rule for a section's rows when a Code, Markdown or Embed block grows and shrinks: they move by the block's rows, keeping the spare rows, never below a block's end. Inferred from CAP-T7THICK.json, no fresh read. These sizes are unread. Last round: the count before any refit stands. Each case's rows are what our code gives from the same start.
rule: s.rows + (block's new rows - its old rows), at least the lowest block's end
padding and corner: T7, for CAP-T7SCRUB: Padding's and Corner's fields have the same <> as Thickness: dim on a hover or a focus, a dark line on focus, a press does nothing, a pull moves the value

count.a section pulled taller: 0 of 3: the pull moved the block's top to row 6 instead and the section stayed at 8. From that start the rows still moved by the block's: 20, 30, 10
count.second code: 0 of 2: the first Code also rose to 18 when the second did, and stayed when the second fell, with the section at 19; ours left the first alone and took the section to 9

third.a section pulled taller, before the bloc: rows move by the block's, so 8 rows pulled up keeps that spare
third.the lowest block: a section's rows move by how far its lowest block's end moves, not the block in hand: that fits Second Code's 19
third.two blocks at the same place: the first rising with the second is read as: a block sharing the risen one's bottom row goes with it on a rise, and neither on a fall
third.blocks not sharing a bottom row: stay where they are, whether side by side, above or below
third.result: Pulled: 16 rows, then the first prediction's 23, 33, 13: right. Lowest block: right in all 30 reads. Sharing a bottom row: wrong. The first also rises when it is taller than the block in hand and shares its columns (Code over Embed), and doesn't when it is shorter (Embed over Code), and side by side nothing moves.

fourth.rule: On a rise by n, a block sharing rows and columns with the risen one, whose end is at or below its end, gets its end moved by n, its top staying. A fall moves no other block. A section's rows move by how far the lowest end moved.
fourth.upper rises, a block wholly under it: that block stays put, since it shares no rows at the start
fourth.upper rises, a block overlapping lower d: that block's end moves by n, its top stays
fourth.lower rises, the upper overlapping: the upper stays: its end is above
fourth.a Code inside a taller Code: the taller one's end moves by n
fourth.a Text the Code overlaps: the same as any block: its end moves by n
fourth.result: Section rows by the lowest end: right, all 22. A Code inside a taller, a Text overlapped with its end above: right. Wrong: a block wholly under the risen one moves with it, top and end, up and down, as under a Video. The two called 'overlapping' share no columns, so they test nothing but the section's rows.

fifth.rule: The line at the block's old end. On a rise by n, a block sharing columns with it: wholly below the line, its top and end move by n; across the line, its end moves. On a fall by n: wholly below the line moves up by n, across it stays. No shared column: stays. A section's rows move by how far the lowest end moved. For every type, as for Video.
fifth.across the line, top inside: end moves on a rise, nothing on a fall
